Considering the love for goats on Voat I think it is fitting to educate /v/aww what a baby goat looks like. Mainly because I have seen allot of lambs being passed on as goats on this subverse.

  • The easiest way to tell a lamb from a goat is by their tails. Sheep tails hang down and are often docked (shortened) for health and sanitary reasons.

  • Goats do not have wool, they have hair.

  • There are color variations in both species. Spots wont make this lamb a goat, being white doesn't make this goat a lamb.

  • Same principle with the horns.

There is a great diversity in both sheep and goats. So there will always be special exemptions, like this Mouflon lamb (A wild sheep that doesn't have a wooly coat). But now you know the basics :)

In Chinese the word for goat and sheep is the same, they don't seem to differentiate.

I think your getting confused by the media's take on the zodiac ''Year of the Sheep' or 'Year of the Goat'?

The zodiac used the word 羊 yáng, there in lies a problem. Look up a Chinese-English dictionary and you will find that yáng means 'sheep'. But yáng does not actually mean 'sheep' at all. Without further qualifiers, yang might mean any such hoofed animal that eats grass and bleats. To find the real meaning, you need to look up a monolingual Chinese dictionary. The definition of yáng is as follows:

  • 山羊 shānyáng ('mountain yáng') = goat
  • 绵羊 miányáng ('cotton yáng') = sheep
  • 羚羊 língyáng = gazelle

Year of the Goat and Year of the Sheep are equally correct because yáng covers both types of animal.
